title: Multi-Factor Authentication
description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) with TOTP authenticator apps, SMS, and backup codes in ASP.NET Core and React.

data.text: **Multi-factor authentication (MFA)** requires users to present two or more verification factors to gain access. Even if a password is compromised, an attacker cannot pass the second factor check.

items: **Something you know**: Password, PIN, security question
**Something you have**: Phone, hardware key, smart card

data.title: NIST Guidance
data.text: NIST SP 800-63B recommends against SMS-based MFA for high-security applications due to SIM-swapping attacks. Prefer TOTP apps or hardware keys.

**TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password)** generates codes that change every 30 seconds. Popular apps include Google Authenticator, Authy, and Microsoft Authenticator. TOTP uses a shared secret and the current timestamp to produce a 6-digit code.

data.title: TOTP Setup with ASP.NET Core Identity

data.text: Users can lose access to their second factor (phone breaks, lost hardware key). **Backup codes** are single-use codes generated during MFA enrollment that users can store securely.

data.title: Generating Backup Codes
data.content: Generating and storing recovery codes for MFA

data.text: SMS sends a numeric code via text message. While convenient, it is vulnerable to **SIM-swapping** attacks where an attacker tricks a carrier into transferring the victim's phone number to a SIM card owned by the attacker.

data.title: SMS Risks
data.text: Avoid SMS MFA for privileged accounts. If you must use SMS, combine it with additional risk signals like device recognition and IP anomaly detection.

data.caption: TOTP-based MFA verification flow
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    participant A as Authenticator App
    U->>A: Scan QR code / enter key
    A->>A: Generate 6-digit code every 30s
    U->>C: Enter password + 6-digit code
    C->>S: POST credentials
    S->>S: Validate password + TOTP
    S->>C: Return session
    C->>U: Logged in

data.text: For trusted devices, you can skip MFA for a limited period. Store a persistent, secure cookie with an encrypted device identifier. If the cookie is missing or invalid, prompt for MFA again.

items.text: Require TOTP or hardware keys over SMS when possible
items.hint: SMS is acceptable for low-risk applications only

items.text: Generate and display recovery codes during MFA enrollment
items.hint: Force users to download or print codes before enabling MFA

items.text: Allow users to manage trusted devices
items.hint: Provide a page to revoke sessions and trusted devices
Never allow admin access without MFA

items.text: Log all MFA successes and failures

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: MFA adds a critical second layer of security
TOTP is the preferred method over SMS
Backup codes prevent lockout when second factors are lost
Hardware keys provide the highest assurance
Always enforce MFA for privileged accounts
data.takeaway: MFA is one of the most effective controls against account takeover.
